summary: Wilson’s two answered assumptions are implemented: drawn-power discard opens an authoritative 2.5-second stacking window; no stack starts the discarder’s power, while a same-rank stack cancels it and makes the stacker the private power actor. Eligible wrong-rank stacks reject with one extra hidden deck card; late/ineligible/self/stale attempts reject without penalty. Original turn/final-turn accounting, Kings, deck-only draws, exchanges, calls and scores are preserved.

window_rule.authority: Server clock for online; local authority clock for solo
window_rule.open: Power discarded from just-drawn deck card enters phase stacking with pendingPower and power null
window_rule.eligibility: Other player of latest discard and now strictly before deadline
window_rule.no_stack: advanceTime(state, now) starts discarder power at or after deadline
window_rule.successful_stack: Cancels pending discarder power; stacker immediately performs same power; window closes
window_rule.testability: reduce accepts injected millisecond now; advanceTime accepts injected now; unit window tests use no timers
window_rule.reason: Single deadline phase is smaller than two-player consent/pass coordination and avoids consent deadlocks

tests: Full Node run: node --test tests/engine.test.mjs tests/boundaries.test.mjs; 44/44 pass, zero failures/skips; includes 1,000-game simulation. Duration 245045.112395ms.

Final-source non-simulation run: node --test --test-skip-pattern='1,000' tests/engine.test.mjs tests/boundaries.test.mjs tests/stack-boundaries.test.mjs; 48/48 selected cases pass, zero failures. Union with simulation: 49 distinct cases (38 engine including simulation, 6 artwork/network boundaries, 5 additional stack boundaries).

1,000 seeded Classic bot games completed: 473561 reducer/clock transitions, 8910 Queen decisions, 8420 Jack swaps, 12434 stacks. Every state checks card conservation and every filtered player view is leak-checked. Counts include injected deadline transitions, not only submitted player actions.

Actual two-client WebSocket integration: 16/16 checks, four rounds, six successful stacks, one rejected wrong-rank stack. Generic stacker error and public hand-size change; penalty faces hidden. Filtered authority equality, stale rejection, reconnect/rematch and forfeit pass.

Focused Python Playwright Chromium: 17/17 checks, two independent network clients, Queen-stack transfer, hidden penalty, cancellation/won-power messages, stacker-only private pair, original turn accounting, overflow and celebration replay. Zero page errors and zero console errors. Two stack-moment screenshots refreshed.
Solo Python Playwright smoke: 7/7 checks, private initial peek/hide and complete solo round; no page errors or horizontal overflow.

npm run check: six Node module syntax checks pass. smoke.py and stack-browser.py compile. Browser QA used exclusive flock -x -w 120 /tmp/chrome.lock, /usr/bin/chromium --no-sandbox and port 5818, never MCP browser. Temporary servers closed and port 5818 confirmed unbound.

Final-source boundary tests additionally cover own ineligible wrong attempt, penalty consuming the last card, empty deck rejection metadata, ordinary replacement power interruption, and caller stealing a final-turn Queen without losing final-turn accounting.
answered_by_wilson: A same-rank power stack cancels discarder power and makes the stacker the acting power player with identical mandatory/optional and private-view rules.
A wrong-rank eligible stack is rejected with one additional unseen deck card.
provisional_choices_and_open_questions: Self-stacking by the latest discarder remains rejected without penalty; Wilson confirmation pending.
The fixed 2500ms power window and retained ordinary placement-to-next-draw window need confirmation, including final-action timing.
Non-power alternating chains remain allowed. A power transfer starts immediately and closes stacking; whether alternating power chains should be supported remains unanswered.
preserved: client/environment.mjs and client/env.css are untouched; SHA-256 checks pass.
Original card artwork, hand-drawn style and environment are intact.
?demo=celebrate still renders a genuine completed simulated match; only its finite replay driver advances the new deadline phase.
Deck-only draws; discard pile never drawn; red King -1 and black King 13 remain non-powers.
Jack mandatory blind swap, Queen mandatory look then optional swap, 7/8 own peek and 9/10 opponent peek keep privacy and skip rules.
Scoring, call rules, exchanges, Quick/Classic, reconnect and chat remain unchanged.
verification_notes: First socket attempt exposed a time-dependent remainingMs view field; it was replaced with stable deadline/windowMs metadata before the successful run.
Socket bot driver was synchronized with timer revisions after an initial harness race; final WebSocket run passed.

Initial focused browser harness wait used CSP-disallowed string evaluation; replaced with the existing evaluate/poll pattern. Successful rerun has zero console/page errors; production CSP was not weakened.
An earlier redundant unit simulation was stopped; only the completed 1,000-game run is claimed.
The final-source fast run covers the later exhaustion-rejection metadata fix; the completed bot simulation never attempts wrong ranks, so its behavior is unaffected by that reporting-only branch.

Physical-device Safari, hostile-host security audit or public deployment.
limitations: Authority knows the deck; solo authority is inspectable. Seeded shuffling is not cryptographic fairness.
Rooms/chat are RAM-only and not end-to-end encrypted; prior in-memory rule states do not migrate.
Current deadlines are absolute server/local authority times; countdown display is advisory, while authoritative timestamp checks decide eligibility.
Historical 23:10/23:17 evidence and reports do not verify this correction.
